sentences: After participating in an extensive archaeological expedition in the Mongolian desert, the archaeologist is in the city to hold a presentation of the findings to his colleagues.
The film material shows how the archaeological team discovered the long sought ancient tomb of an Emperor of an ancient dynasty.
In the tomb, the team found a scroll, telling of a secret fire temple.
The temple is believed to be hiding a previously unknown oil reserve, and would be of great financial importance to the Chinese people were it to be discovered.
During the expedition, when the tomb was opened, a forceful hurricane took the life of one crewman, the co-pilot.
The storm was predicted by an ancient curse guarding the tomb.
Unfortunately, as the archaeologist is about to reveal the contents of the scroll during the presentation, he starts choking and ultimately dies from suffocation.
After the presentation, it turns out that the scroll is missing from the archaeologist's safe in his office, and his secretary claims she has no knowledge of its whereabouts.

One of the archaeologist's students, the student, does his own investigation into the death of his professor, and finds out that the archaeologist must have been poisoned with what another man, the friend, identifies as an oriental vegetable poison.
The student finds a pitcher and a glass cup containing traces of this poison.
Another member of the expedition team, the camera man, is attacked in his home, and is found injured by the student and the friend.
They also find the secretary tied up and gagged at the house, having been attacked after entering the house.
They are both unaware that the co-pilot faked his own death at the tomb, and that he and the archaeologist's butler are planning to lay their hands on all artifacts found in the tomb.
The friend manages to trace the camera man's attacker to a hideout near the waterfront, where both the co-pilot and the butler are hiding.
The co-pilot escapes through a secret door, but the student and the friend find an artifact identifiable from the tomb.
They also find the butler's dead body in a coffin, and it turns out he has been poisoned, then stabbed.
The two amateur sleuths manage to get an article published in the paper, saying the co-pilot is sick with yellow fever in a hospital, to lure the killer there.
The student wears a wire and impersonates the co-pilot at the hospital.
The co-pilot himself turns up at the hospital, and also the camera man.
The student and the co-pilot fight each other, but the friend and the police interrupt them.
It turns out the camera man has worked together with the co-pilot, but tried to double-cross him and break into the archaeologist's safe to steal the scroll.
The camera man also killed the archaeologist to keep the secret of the oil reserve to himself.
He later killed the butler.
The original scroll has now been destroyed by the camera man, but there is still a photo of it left.
After the camera man is arrested, the photo is given to the Chinese government so that they can try to find the oil reserve.
The gang of the big-shot theater-district gambler, at a restaurant, plays with military toys, imagining fighting the enemy dictator.
The restaurant gives the gambler a cheesecake not made by the baker, a baker who makes the gambler's favorite cheesecake, and the gambler is unhappy.
His mother tells him the baker, her neighbor, is missing and she's "got a feeling" something sinister has happened.
The gambler searches the bakery and finds the baker's dead body.
A young singer quickly leaves the shop upon hearing about the baker's demise.
His mother believes that the girl knows something and tracks her down to a night club, where she creates a racket by "crabbing" about the baker's death.
The club owner, co-owner of the club, calls the gambler, insisting that he come down and take care of the situation.
While at the club, the gambler has a drink with the singer that is interrupted by her piano player, who takes her away to a back room, where he shoots the club owner's partner.
The singer and the piano player then disappear in a taxi as the gambler stumbles upon the partner.
Before dying, the partner raises up five fingers to indicate who took the singer.
The gambler quickly leaves to search for the singer, inadvertently leaving one of his gloves at the murder scene.
While being suspected of the partner's murder by the club owner and the police, the gambler traces the taxi to an antiques auction house operated by the auctioneer and his assistant, a woman.
The gambler poses as a bidder but is recognized by the piano player.
The gambler sees the singer and trusts her, but she subsequently knocks him out; he is tied up and left in a storage room with one of his boys, the sidekick, who was captured earlier.
Later, the singer visits them and helps them break free before they can be shipped out in crates.
While escaping, the gambler and the sidekick walk into a room with maps, charts, a short-wave radio, and a portrait of the enemy dictator.
They realize what the partner was indicating before he died: their captors are "fivers" or enemy fifth columnists.
The gambler finds a notebook and reads the baker's name in it as well as that of the singer, her Jewish name, and the death of her father in a concentration camp.
With the singer in tow, they escape.
They are chased by the auctioneer and his cronies into the city park.
Here, the singer explains that she works with the auctioneer only to save her father's life.
While the gambler fights with an enemy agent, the singer reads the torn-out page that states her father is already dead.
The gambler and the singer go to the police, who search the antique house, but find it empty.
Not believing the gambler's story, they attempt to arrest him, but he escapes by diving into the river.
He arrives at his lawyer's apartment, only to have the club owner and his mob break in, eager to avenge the partner's murder.
After the gambler convinces them of his innocence, the two gangs join forces against the enemy spies.
The gambler, the sidekick, and another of his boys go to the police station where the singer is being held.
The auctioneer, however, has bailed her out, and they arrive as she is being forced into a car.
Following the car, they find a large underground enemy meeting.
The gambler and the sidekick capture two enemy agents and impersonate them to get in, but the explosives expert the gambler is impersonating is asked to report on his work.
The gambler and the sidekick stall the meeting using a double talk ruse until the combined gangs arrive to break it up.
The auctioneer escapes, asking the piano player to join him in a suicide attack to blow up a battleship in the city harbor.
The piano player refuses, so the auctioneer kills him and proceeds alone.
The gambler follows him to the docks, but the auctioneer surprises him and forces him into a motorboat containing high explosives.
At gunpoint, the auctioneer forces the gambler to steer the boat toward the battleship.
The gambler suddenly steers the boat off course and jumps into the water, while the boat with the auctioneer still on board crashes into a barge loaded with lumber and explodes.
Back at the police station, the gambler and the singer find out that all charges have been dropped and that the mayor is going to honor him at city hall.
His mother enters complaining that the milkman has disappeared, and as before, she's "got a feeling" about it.

Aboard a ship, the newspaper reporter falls for the passenger and meets her uncle, who is in possession of a small wooden chest that he believes could be a copy made by the mysterious copyist, a notorious art forger.
A police inspector, the colonel, is also aboard, presumably on the copyist's tail.
The reporter proposes to the passenger and meets her relatives and family acquaintances.
They include the noblewoman, the chest's rightful owner, whose maid had been trying to retrieve it because a secret drawer contained compromising love letters.
A police constable arrives and the reporter contacts the colonel as well.
The uncle and another guest quickly end up dead and the colonel quickly declares everyone in the house to be a suspect.
A second hidden compartment contains priceless diamonds.
The reporter and the passenger realize just in time that the colonel is the copyist who has been pursuing the jewels all along.

In the beginning of the film, the detective is in a foreign city, along with his son, and the local chief of police, the police chief, to arrest the singer, whom the detective suspects killed a man in the island city.
After a performance, the singer's boyfriend asks her to marry him, which she accepts.
Her personal assistant then reminds the singer she has an appointment with a Hindu psychic.
The singer visits the psychic, who puts her in a semi-comatose state using coffee and cigarettes laced with a special natural herb.
The singer reveals in this state that she did kill a man, after he refused to marry her in the island city.
The psychic records the conversation.
When the singer wakes up, the psychic tells her what she told him, but assures her that it will be kept confidential between them.
On the way home, the worried singer convinces the boyfriend to elope instead of marrying at a later date.
When she arrives home, she begins packing.
Later, the detective, the son, and the police chief arrive at the singer's house to arrest her, but instead find her dead in her room.
The three conclude that the singer was murdered, and spot many obvious clues which they realize were left there on purpose to throw them off.
They also notice the singer's jewelry missing.
The detective then informs the singer's guests, who were there to celebrate her engagement, of her death, and brings in two suspects, the psychic and the second man.
The second man reveals that he was married to the singer, but they had separated.
The psychic plays back his conversation with the singer, and reveals himself to be the brother of the man the singer killed.
The police chief asks everyone to stay in the house while the murder is being investigated.
Later, the son witnesses a conversation between the singer's butler and maid.
The butler tells the maid to stay quiet about something she saw earlier.
The detective and the police chief find scratch marks on the floor where the singer was murdered.
The detective suspects that the scratch marks were from the brooch the singer was wearing, and that a pin on that brooch would still be stuck in the murderer's shoe.
The detective then finds similar scratch marks under one of the chairs at the dinner table where all of the guests had dined.
The son hides in the butler's room and finds the singer's jewelry there.
He then takes the butler to the detective.
The butler explains that he has the jewels but did not kill the singer.
Before he can tell the detective who did, the lights go out and he is shot.
The detective then asks all of the guests to go back to their original positions at the dinner table.
He reveals to them that the scratch marks he found were under the assistant's chair.
When the assistant protests her innocence, the detective suggests the psychic put her in the semi-comatose state.
When she still says she did not kill the singer, the detective asks that he go under the same treatment using the same cigarette.
But when he does, the detective is unaffected.
The psychic tries to admit to killing the singer, but the assistant stops him, revealing she did it.
She further explains that she was the wife of the murdered man.
After hearing of the psychic's conversation with the singer, the assistant learned the singer was going to elope.
Realizing that the singer was going to leave and escape justice, the assistant killed her.
When the butler walked in on the act, she offered him the jewels to keep him quiet, and later shot him.
The police chief then arrests the assistant and takes her to jail.
The son asks to take the maid back to the island city with him, but the detective tells him he has been drafted in the army.
The young woman is impatient for the sale of her statue of a Roman emperor, as she needs the money to help her sick brother.
The dealer, one of the art dealers handling the auction, asks her to stay away, claiming that an emotional attachment to the work might cause her to make a scene.
She shows up anyway, and notices that the statue is not hers, but a fake.
When the dealer pulls out a gun to silence her, the reformed thief spots him and fires his own pistol.
The young woman is only grazed, but the dealer accidentally kills his partner and the replica's sculptor, the forger.
When the police inspector arrives, he automatically assumes that the reformed thief is guilty and takes him into custody.
The dealer hides in the hollow fake statue.
Then when the coast is clear, he puts the forger's body (and the incriminating bullet) inside and makes his escape.
The replica is purchased by the reformed thief's wealthy friend, the millionaire.
Despite lacking a corpse, the police inspector keeps the reformed thief in jail, but not for long.
The reformed thief switches places with an ice cream man and escapes.
He goes to see the young woman in the hospital to obtain information.
To get in undetected, he once again appropriates the unlucky ice cream man's uniform and pretends to be the young woman's doctor.
When he learns why she needs the money so badly, he arranges for his assistant, the little sidekick, to masquerade as an insurance adjuster to give her $6000 he borrowed from the millionaire.
The money had initially been intended to pay off a blackmailing schemer, who claims she is the reformed thief's wife.
When the schemer shows up and demands the money, the young woman realizes that the reformed thief is her benefactor.
The dealer arranges to buy the statue from the unsuspecting millionaire.
The reformed thief learns about it, and sees a way to unravel the mystery.
He follows the movers back to their lair.
Sneaking inside, he overpowers a thug, one of the dealer's henchmen.
However, the dealer returns, with the young woman as his prisoner, resulting in a Mexican standoff.
Meanwhile, both the millionaire and the little sidekick are picked up by the police.
The police inspector has them released, hoping they will lead him to their friend.
The little sidekick is too experienced to be taken in, but the millionaire does return to the crooks' secret underground workshop, where they copy artworks.
In the ensuing gunfight, the dealer is killed, but the shots destroy the electrical circuits controlling the only way in, trapping them all in the soundproof chamber.
The reformed thief comes up with the idea to start a fire in the ventilation shaft, and firemen arrive to let them out.
The young medic, a med student, operates on the young woman, victim of a vehicular accident, saving her life.
Later, the young medic opens a medical practice with buddies the ambitious doctor and the third doctor.
Even though the young medic woos the young woman, she falls for the ambitious doctor.
The ambitious doctor purchases some much-needed medical supplies on the black market from the scarred gangster and his bodyguard, the gunman.
When the gunman is shot during a shake-down attempt, the ambitious doctor cares for him.
The gunman is arrested and the ambitious doctor defends him at trial, claiming he fixed an acid burn and not a gunshot wound.
The young medic, who has a side job working for the medical examiner's office, discovers that most of his clients are thugs sent to the doctor's office by the gangster.
He realizes that the ambitious doctor lied in court.
The gangster murders the shake-down victim, who tells the cops before he dies that a "man with a scar on his face" shot him.
The gangster forces the ambitious doctor to remove the gangster's facial scar or get exposed as a gangland doctor.
The ambitious doctor does so, but takes photos of the operation that documents what he's done.
The young woman walks in as the surgery is ending, and realizes her beau is in league with a criminal element.
The gangster goes on trial.
The ambitious doctor sends his photos to the young medic, who is forced by a judge to admit that the ambitious doctor was the source of the images.
The ambitious doctor, realizing his future is finished no matter what, testifies in court against the gangster.
The gangster is found guilty, and the gunman shoots the ambitious doctor when he leaves the courtroom.
The gunman himself is then killed by the cops.
The young medic, the third doctor, and the young woman mourn the ambitious doctor.
The private investigator and his singer fiancée hear a woman screaming from a room in their hotel.
The hotel maid has discovered two dead people - the producer, owner of the hotel and the adjoining theater, and the actress, one of the producer's actresses.
Both are dressed in medieval costumes, and the producer is wearing the head from a dog costume.
The police investigator arrives at the scene and learns from the hotel manager that the costumes are from the producer's only successful show, a musical revue, from many years earlier.
The actress had been the show's leading lady, and the comic actor played the dog character.
The private investigator suspects the comic actor because of the dog-costume head on the producer.
The older actor, also an actor in the producer's show, tells the police that the producer had hosted a private party for the entire cast to celebrate its anniversary.
The private investigator examines the list of those involved in the production and discovers that the musical director was the conductor, an alcoholic who also lives at the hotel.
As the investigation proceeds, the private investigator learns that the producer kept another woman in addition to the actress and that the apartment has many entrances and exits.
From the older actor's daughter, he learns that the cast member stole money from the producer, so he visits the cast member and finds him with the widow, the producer's wife.
They confess to embezzling money from the producer, but claim to be innocent of his murder.
They hire the private investigator to help them prove their innocence.
The private investigator continues his investigation and talks to the conductor.
He learns that the comic actor died in World War I in a foreign country, but then discovers a letter from the comic actor in the actress's room that proves that the comic actor is still alive.
The private investigator brings the cast member to the producer's apartment, and they discover a hidden passage to the maid's room downstairs.
They find the maid's dead body and a note explaining that she had killed the producer because he had betrayed her years earlier for another woman.
The maid was once known as an actress under another name.
The private investigator does not believe that the maid has killed herself, so he continues searching for the killer.
When the private investigator is back in the producer's apartment, the police investigator is knocked unconscious in the next room by the conductor.
The theater doorman arrives and confesses that he killed the producer and the actress.
He is really the comic actor, and he was married to the actress before she had left him for the producer.
He also killed the maid because she had discovered too much about him.
The conductor has been blackmailing the comic actor, whom he saw leaving the apartment right after the killings.
While they are talking, the police investigator regains consciousness, and together with the private investigator, he overpowers the doorman and the conductor.

The private investigator asks the police investigator to be his best man at the wedding later in the day, but the private investigator then learns that his fiancée has eloped with her ex-boyfriend because she grew tired of waiting for the private investigator.
The novelist appears to have a normal life handling investments, but secretly he writes lurid detective novels under a pseudonym.
His other career is unknown to his wife or to anyone but the inspector, who mocks the books, insisting that true crime is much more difficult to solve.
The novelist's latest book is controversial, parodying members of a women's club, using names that thinly disguise real members, which include his wife and her mother.
The pseudonymous author sent copies of his book to every woman in the club.
Indignant, his wife and her mother tell the novelist that the club has decided to sue for libel.
Privately, the novelist advises the lawyer that the lawsuit would bring more publicity for the book, urging him to lie to the women and keep postponing any action.
The lawyer deplores deceit, but the novelist points out that the lawyer has been married four times to his one.
The novelist counsels that a happy marriage depends on being considerate, keeping things from one's wife that would make her unhappy.
A smuggler attempts to blackmail the novelist to help him turn uncut diamonds into cash; otherwise, he will reveal the novelist's secret life to the public.
When the smuggler is found dead on a yacht, the coroner and police think he died of heart failure caused by alcoholism.

When the novelist insists that the smuggler was murdered for the diamonds without disclosing prior contact between them, the inspector and the police detective challenge the novelist to solve the “murder” before the police.
Ticket stubs in the smuggler's jacket pocket lead the novelist to the burlesque dancer, who becomes his prime suspect.
Under an assumed identity as "the cowboy", the novelist romances the dancer for information.
The dancer's dentist, however, gives her a solid alibi.
When his wife catches the novelist sneaking home at 2:30 from a "business meeting", she becomes sure that the novelist is having an affair and hires a private detective.
The detective finds out that the novelist has been seeing the dancer and reveals that the novelist has a secret (writing) studio that they believe is for liaisons.
His wife goes to see the dancer at her burlesque show.
Meanwhile, the dancer asks "the cowboy" to retrieve a suitcase from a locker.

After the inspector receives a call from the federal investigators, informing him that the smuggler was involved with a diamond smuggling ring, the inspector orders another autopsy on the body, but the coroner informs him that it has been cremated.
The inspector and the police detective begin to suspect that the novelist murdered the smuggler for the diamonds.
The novelist locates the locker and finds diamonds in the suitcase.

When the dancer fails to turn up at a rendezvous with "the cowboy" or at a rehearsal, the novelist, the inspector, and the police detective converge on the dancer's apartment and find her fatally shot.
Meanwhile, the dentist arrives, claiming he was working in his office in the building but did not hear any gunshots.

A creditor who was surveying the dancer's apartment saw a woman who lost a heel from her shoe leaving the dancer's apartment, and a taxi driver says he dropped the woman off on the street where the novelist lives.
At home, the novelist finds his wife's shoe is missing a heel, and his wife admits to finding the dancer's body before leaving immediately.
Initially, his wife thinks the novelist killed the dancer, while the novelist believes his wife killed her.
The police detective arrives with the taxi driver and reveals that the novelist is the pseudonymous author.
His wife and her mother are certain that they will be stricken from the social register.
The police detective accuses the novelist and his wife of killing the dancer and the smuggler for the diamonds, but the novelist evades arrest and sets off to find the real killer.

The novelist concludes that the dentist is the dancer's accomplice, who provided the poison to kill the smuggler while the dancer got the smuggler drunk so alcohol would make the poison hard to detect in an autopsy.
The dentist attempts to kill the novelist, but the inspector and the police detective arrive and arrest the novelist despite his protests.
Taking his opportunity, the dentist absconds in his car, but then hears on the radio that the novelist fell off a roof to his death while escaping from custody.
Thinking himself safe, the dentist returns to his office, where the novelist, the inspector, and the police detective await to apprehend him.
The inspector calls the novelist to help out on a new murder case, and his wife insists on joining him, without her mother's knowledge.
The sleuth, a ladies' man and amateur crime solver known by a nickname, reluctantly agrees to give up both habits to mollify his fiancée.
He and his uncouth sidekick become unenthusiastic stockbrokers.
When his fiancée asks him to attend a party given by the hostess to mingle with potential clients, he refuses.
However, when the hostess asks for his help via her pretty assistant, he cannot resist.
It seems that the hostess's soirées have been plagued by jewel thefts and she is particularly worried about the diamond of her guest.
At the party, his fiancée becomes annoyed when she realises why the sleuth changed his mind about attending and retaliates by dancing with a suave stranger.
In frustration, she grabs the flower from the suave stranger's lapel and flings it at the sleuth.
He calmly picks it up and attaches it to his lapel.
The guest then insists on dancing with the sleuth; she hands him her diamond secretly, much to his puzzlement, then leaves the room.
Moments later, a shot rings out and the guest is dead.
The killer is seen by the sidekick as he makes his getaway.
Two police detectives take the sidekick to the police station on suspicion of murder.
The sleuth persuades the inspector to release the sidekick so he can flush out the real murderer.
Then he and the assistant go to see the hostess, leaving the sidekick in the car.
While they are gone, the sidekick is abducted by the gunman, the guest's killer.
The gunman orders the sidekick to call the sleuth to offer to trade the sidekick's life for the diamond.
However, the gunman is shot and once again, the sidekick is found by the police near a dead body.
By this point, the sleuth suspects the guest arranged to have her diamond "stolen" so she could collect on the insurance.
The flower was a signal, indicating to whom the guest was to give the jewel.
It should have been the suave stranger.
The sleuth and the assistant break into his apartment but have to hide when the suave stranger enters.
He realizes someone has been there and opens a secret compartment to check if it has been found.
Relieved, he leaves the room.
The sleuth sneaks in and takes a gun he finds in the compartment, fairly certain it was used to shoot the gunman.
The police confirm it is the murder weapon.
Meanwhile, the sleuth calls his fiancée to warn her to stay away from the suave stranger but she believes he is lying out of jealousy and tells the suave stranger so.
Forewarned, the suave stranger goes to the sleuth's apartment, ties up his servant and demands the diamond at gunpoint when the sleuth returns.
He is frightened off when he mistakes the assistant at the door for the police.
Now certain about his theory, the sleuth goes to see the hostess, taking the inspector along.
She tells them she has been receiving threats, so they stand guard in the living room while she sleeps.
The suave stranger enters through her bedroom window but when he lunges at her, the sleuth and the inspector charge in.
They are puzzled when the suave stranger collapses and dies.
Then the sleuth finds a hypodermic needle on the floor.
The sleuth stops the hostess from stepping on it and destroying the incriminating fingerprints.
He reveals that she, her husband the gunman and the suave stranger were responsible for the thefts.
The hostess and the gunman decided to betray the suave stranger but he found out.
The sleuth realized she must be involved when the sidekick was kidnapped; nobody else knew where the sidekick was at the time.
A disparate group of individuals are in a room; some are gambling, some are drinking coffee, others are chatting as if at a party.
Curtains are removed from the windows to reveal bars.
The group is in a prison to witness the execution of the condemned man, a hard core murderer.
The condemned man is told there has been no commutation of his execution.

Having never given a confession, the condemned man proceeds to tell the crowd of the true events of what happened as his benefactor promised him his release; but then falls over dead, the victim of a poison dart.

The district attorney conducts a search of the occupants of the room and together with his girlfriend the crime reporter and his young receptionist solve the murder and the criminal mastermind behind the condemned man.
The district attorney searches everyone in the room for the murder weapon, then has everyone return to the same seats in which they sat before the condemned man's murder.
The district attorney becomes suspicious of an elderly man, the condemned man's character witness, because he has a cigarette holder which could be used as a dart blower.
The elderly man proclaims his innocence but is arrested.
The reporter, meanwhile, is sent to the prison, and the district attorney asks her to get acquainted with the appointee, a parole board appointee.
After the district attorney is reprimanded for arresting the elderly man, whom he admits is an unlikely suspect, he asks the reporter to interview the condemned man's girl friend, the sweetheart.
The sweetheart defends her former boyfriend, but admits that he made a phone call from her apartment on the day of the murder.
The sweetheart only remembers part of the number, and shortly after the reporter leaves, the sweetheart gets a threatening phone call.
The district attorney sends the police detective to watch the sweetheart, and recognizes the telephone number as the appointee's.
The district attorney is then mystified by a code written on the back of the appointee's business card, and asks the receptionist, a switchboard operator who wants to be a detective, to decipher it.
The district attorney questions the appointee and he denies knowing the condemned man.
But his butler admits to having placed bets with the condemned man.
The sweetheart, meanwhile, plans to leave town and demands that the activist.
The activist, the head of an organization which opposes capital punishment, return the money she gave him to obtain the condemned man's release.
The activist, who was at the execution, accompanies the sweetheart to the bank, but she dies suddenly after honking the car horn.
The police detective catches the activist when he runs, and the district attorney later discovers a poisoned dart embedded in the steering wheel that matches the one that killed the condemned man.
The district attorney arrests the activist and frees the elderly man.
One evening, the reporter and the colleague, a fellow reporter, dine at the restaurateur's café, where the reporter's check is refused.
The appointee comes in shortly after and, because he is friendly with the restaurateur, offers to help.
A waiter accepts the appointee's check and takes it to the restaurateur's office.
The restaurateur burns the appointee's check, and gives the waiter a roll of money.
The appointee then gives the money to the reporter, but still pays her bill.
Later, while waiting for the district attorney at his office, the reporter realizes that the code on the appointee's business card is for a library book.
As the receptionist is asking the investigative department to find out about the book, the reporter accidentally drops her purse.
The reporter and the receptionist are shocked to discover five $500 bills in her wallet, sandwiched between two one-dollar bills.
When the district attorney returns, the receptionist tells him what transpired.
The appointee becomes the district attorney's new suspect after he learns that a library book on toxicology was checked out by the butler.

The receptionist arranges for the district attorney and the colleague to listen in on a telephone conversation between the restaurateur and the appointee, who are partners in a protection racket, during which they hear that the restaurateur believed the money was intended for the appointee.
At that moment, the appointee reveals that the reporter is with him, and the district attorney, the colleague and the police detective rush to his house.
The district attorney bursts into the appointee's office just as he is about to kill the reporter with a poisoned dart.
The appointee confesses to the murders of both the condemned man and the sweetheart, then tries to kill the district attorney.
However, the reporter knocks the appointee out with a vase, and the colleague and the police detective capture the restaurateur and his thugs.
The district attorney and the reporter embrace, and the district attorney asks her to join his staff permanently.
